text: Preliminary pages, written in British English, are arranged: Title page; Certification; Approval page; Dedication (if any); Acknowledgements; Abstract; Table of Contents; List of Tables, Figures, Plates (if any); List of Abbreviations; List of Symbols (if any); Tables of Cases/Statutes/International Instruments (Law only); Operational definition of terms. All preliminary headings are in upper case and each appears on a separate page.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section A 1, p. 1

text: The title page carries the title, the author's name with registration number, the thesis statement, and the month and year of completion. The title is as brief as possible (maximum 21 words), accurate and descriptive, typed in bold capitals; avoid phrases like 'a report on investigations into'. Names are written forenames then surname. The month-and-year line is no more than 25 mm from the foot of the page. The thesis statement reads: 'A Thesis submitted to the Department of …, Faculty of …, Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, in partial fulfillment of the requirements for the degree of …'. Title page uses 1.5 line spacing.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section A 1.1, pp. 2-3

text: Certification is a formal statement that the candidate is responsible for the submitted work, which is original and not submitted elsewhere (specimen in Appendix A2). The Approval page carries names, signatures and dates of the supervisor(s), Head of Department, External Examiner, Dean of Faculty and Dean of the School of Postgraduate Studies (specimen in Appendix A3). Both use 1.5 line spacing.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section A 1.2-1.3, p. 3; Appendices A2-A3, pp. 43-44

text: The dedication is a brief tribute. Acknowledgements thank God first, then supervisor(s), Head of Department, department staff, Dean of Faculty, family and friends, and note financial assistance or special facilities. Acknowledgements are written in the third person singular and are not endorsed by the candidate. Both use 1.5 line spacing.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section A 1.4-1.5, p. 3

text: The abstract is an informative summary of at most 250 words (postgraduate diploma), 300 words (Master's thesis) or 500 words (doctoral dissertation). It outlines the purpose, research methods and procedure, major results and conclusions, and recommendations. It starts with a topic sentence stating the major theme, and is written in one block paragraph. 1.5 line spacing.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section A 1.6, p. 4

text: The table of contents is on a separate sheet, follows the structure and headings of the write-up, contains only the first four levels of headings, and includes page numbers. It is double spaced (2.0). A typical contents page is Appendix A4.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section A 1.7, p. 4; Appendix A4, p. 45

text: Chapter One (Introduction) has segments: Background to the Study; Statement of the Problem; Aim/Purpose of the Study; Research Objectives (itemised); Rationale for/Relevance of the Study and Justification for the Study (where applicable); Significance of the Study; Scope of the Study; Research Questions and Research Hypotheses (where applicable). For Arts and Education, purpose and objectives may be one heading. Double spaced (2.0). Project decision: a combined heading such as 'Aim and Objectives of the Study' is accepted in place of separate Aim/Purpose and Research Objectives headings (the Manual itself permits this only for Arts and Education; the supervisor approved it for this project).
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section B 2.1, pp. 5-8

text: Chapter Two (Literature Review) has: Conceptual Framework (shown in a sketch) and Theoretical Framework (where applicable); Theoretical Studies (where applicable); Empirical Studies, organised under sub-headings by major issues and synthesised, never by presenting each work's abstract in a paragraph; and a Summary of Literature Review showing what has been done and the research gaps.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section B 2.2, pp. 8-9

text: For Computer Science theses the SECTION STRUCTURE of Chapter Three follows the department format, not this list. Content guidance that still applies: describe procedures in enough detail for another person to replicate them, state and justify any modification to standard methods, and describe sampling and data analysis. Chapter Three is Materials and Methods (science-based), or Methods/Methodology (humanities-based). Science-based: study area, materials used, experimental design, laboratory procedure detailed enough for replication, sampling technique, statistical analysis. Humanities-based: research design, area, population, sample and sampling technique, instrument, validity, reliability, method of data collection, method of data analysis. Modifications to standard methods must be stated and justified.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section B 2.3, pp. 9-12

text: For Computer Science theses the SECTION STRUCTURE of Chapter Four follows the department format. Content guidance that still applies: results in the third person; discussion interprets findings in light of the literature and the objectives; do not duplicate table data in a graph; derived data go in the Appendix. Results and Discussion are presented in the third person, using tables, figures or plates. Discussion interprets the significance of findings in light of existing literature and the stated objectives. Data shown in a table must not be duplicated in a graph, and data from which tables or graphs were derived go in the Appendix.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section B 2.4, pp. 12-13

text: For Computer Science theses the SECTION STRUCTURE of Chapter Five follows the department format. Content guidance that still applies: findings are itemised and show the contribution to knowledge; the conclusion is a logical judgment based on the major findings and the problem the research set out to address; recommendations are based on findings.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section B 2.5, pp. 13-14

text: Cite the author's surname, a comma, then the year: (Eze, 1997). When the name is part of the sentence, only the year is parenthesised: Okeke (2014) found… Works by the same author in the same year take suffixes a, b, c.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.1.1, p. 15

section: In-text citation — two to five authors
text: Two authors are joined by 'and', never an ampersand (&), and both are named every time: Ifeanyi and Ossai (2008). Three to five authors: name all at first citation, then the first author plus et al. (italic) and year. More than five authors: first author plus et al., comma, year, in every citation; the reference list names all authors.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.1.2(i)-(iii), pp. 15-16

section: In-text citation — multiple and secondary sources
text: Works cited together are arranged alphabetically: (Nkamigbo, 2018; Nwankwo, 1998; Okoye, 2005). A work cited through a secondary source: only the secondary source is dated and listed in the references: (Uchenna, cited in Nkamigbo, 2019).
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.1.2(iv), p. 16

text: Editorials cite the periodical title and year; other anonymous articles cite 'Anonymous' and year. Corporate authors are cited by official name and year; the name may be abbreviated after first full mention. Authors with the same surname are distinguished by initials: N. Nwaiwu (2015). Laws are cited by approved title and year of enactment.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.1.3-3.1.6, pp. 16-18

section: In-text citation — personal communication and electronic media
text: Personal communications (interviews, letters, e-mails) are cited in the text with the communicator's initials, surname and date but are not listed in References: (D.C. Omeje, personal communication, January 14, 2017). Broadcast news, programmes and films are cited by title and date, or director and date.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.1.7-3.1.8, pp. 18-20

text: A quotation matches the original exactly in wording, spelling and punctuation and gives source and page (Borden, 1980:23). Under two lines: in double quotation marks. More than forty words: set off by indentation and single spaced. Omitted material is shown by three dots only.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.2, pp. 20-21

text: References are placed at the end and listed alphabetically by first author's surname. Each reference is single spaced with double spacing between references. Science, Education, Management and Social Science works list only references actually cited under the heading References; some Arts disciplines may use a Bibliography including uncited works. Works by the same author are in chronological order, with a, b, c suffixes for the same year.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.3.1-3.3.2, pp. 21-22

text: Author, A.A. (Year). Title of work in italics, sentence case. City: Publisher. Example: Arinze-Umobi, C. (2008). Domestic violence against women in Nigeria: A legal anatomy. Onitsha: Folmech Printing & Pub. Co. Ltd. Multiple authors are joined by 'and'. E-books and database books add 'Retrieved from URL or doi, on (date accessed)'.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.3.3, pp. 22-23

text: Chapter in an edited book: Surname, A. (Year). Chapter title. In A. Editor (Ed), Book title italic. Place: Publisher, PP.x-y. Reports and pamphlets: Surname, A. (Year). Title italic. Edition. Place: Publisher, pages (series). Laws: code and year, italic title, enacting government, gazette number.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.3.3(iv)-3.3.5, pp. 23-25

text: Author, A.A. (Year). Title of article. Title of Journal, Volume (Issue), PP-PP. Online articles add doi or 'Retrieved from journal URL, on (date accessed)'. Example: Nkamigbo, L.C. (2011). Experimental analysis of voicing contrast in Igbo. UNIZIK Journal of Arts and Humanities, 12(2), 189-203.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.3.8, pp. 27-28

text: Unpublished theses: Surname, A. (Year). Title. Unpublished PhD Dissertation / Master's thesis, Department, University, Place, pages. Conference papers: Surname, A. (Year). Title. A paper presented at [event] organized by …, held at [venue], [dates].
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.3.6-3.3.9, pp. 25-28

text: Magazine: Author (Year, Month). Title. Magazine, Volume(Issue), PP xx-xx. Newspaper: Author (Year, Month Day). Title. Newspaper, p.15. Page numbers are preceded by P or PP. Websites: Author (Year, Month Day). Title. Retrieved from URL, on (date accessed). Interviews: Okoye, B.O. (2014, October 18). Personal Interview.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section C 3.3.11-3.3.16, pp. 29-32

text: The work is typed in Times New Roman, size 12, with double (2.0) line spacing. Paper is A4 (approximately 21.0 cm x 29.7 cm), at least 80 g/m2, one side only. Paragraphs are indented from the sixth space. The title page, certification, approval, dedication, acknowledgements, abstract and cover page use 1.5 spacing; the table of contents and chapters use double spacing.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section D 4.1(i)-(iii),(vi),(viii), p. 35

text: Left margin 2.5 cm and right margin 2.0 cm. On the first page of each chapter the heading is 5.0 cm below the top edge of the paper and the last sentence is 2.0 cm from the bottom edge; on other pages the first sentence is 2.0 cm from the top edge and the last sentence 2.0 cm from the bottom edge.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section D 4.1(iv)-(v), p. 35

text: All pages are numbered at the bottom right, for both preliminary pages and main body. Preliminary pages use Roman numerals (i, ii, …); the body text uses Arabic numerals (1, 2, …).
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section D 4.1(vii), p. 35

text: Chapter number: centred, bold, uppercase. Chapter title directly below, centred, bold, uppercase. Level two (4.1): bold, flush left, first letter of each word capitalised except conjunctions. Level three (4.1.1): bold, flush left, only the first word capitalised. Level four (4.1.1.1): bold, italic, flush left, only the first word capitalised. Arabic numerals number headings; Roman numerals are for itemisation only.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section D 4.2, pp. 35-37

text: Tables are numbered by chapter (Table 4.1) in order of first mention, double spaced regardless of length. The word Table and number are flush left above the table; the title is flush left with principal words capitalised. Column headings are centred. Horizontal rules separate title, headings and body; avoid vertical rules. Tables must be understandable without the text, inserted just after first mention, and discussed in the text. Long tables or tables from other sources go in Appendices.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section D 4.3.1, pp. 37-38

text: Figures (graphs, charts, drawings, diagrams, maps) are numbered with Arabic numerals; photographs are Plates numbered with Roman numerals. Captions go below, flush left: 'Figure 4.1.' Avoid phrases like 'Graph showing…'. Data used for graphs and charts go in appendices, not text tables.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section D 4.3.2-4.4, pp. 38-39

text: Numerals under 10 are spelled out unless a unit of measurement; positions are written 'Fifth', not 5th. Dates are '15 December, 2005' and decades '1990s' with no apostrophe. Do not mix % with spelled figures. SI units are used; units are spelled out when alone and abbreviated when qualified by numbers or in tables and figures.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section D 4.5, pp. 39-40

text: Define terms that are field-specific, that have everyday meanings that could confuse, or that relate to the research; list them in the preliminary pages. Scientific names are italicised. Every acronym is spelled out on first appearance followed by the abbreviation in parentheses. Standard Latin abbreviations are not used in the text, except et al. (and vs. for Law), both italicised.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section D 4.6-4.8, pp. 40-41

text: The cover page shows, in upper case Times New Roman 14: title; name of student (surname last); Department/Faculty/University; month and year corrections were certified. 1.5 line spacing.
source: UNIZIK Manual of Style (2019), Section D 4.9, p. 41

text: Chapter Three: Methodology and System Analysis — 3.1 Methodology Adopted; 3.2 System Analysis; 3.2.1 Analysis of the Existing System; 3.2.1.1 Weaknesses of the Existing System; 3.2.2 Analysis of the Proposed System (detailed analysis with illustrations); 3.2.2.1 Advantages of the Proposed System; 3.2.2.2 High Level Model of the Proposed System. The methodology determines the diagrams: SSADM expects a Data Flow Diagram and Entity-Relationship Diagram; OOADM expects DFD, use case, interaction, sequence, activity, collaboration and package diagrams. Diagrams are labelled and numbered.
source: Computer Science MSc/PhD Documentation Format, Chapter Three

text: Chapter Four: System Design and Implementation — 4.1 Objectives of the Design; 4.2 Control Centre/Main Menu; 4.3 The Submenus/Subsystems; 4.4 System Specifications (choose those applicable: database development tool, database design and structure, math specification, program module specification, input/output format, algorithm, data dictionary); 4.5 System Flowchart (if any); 4.6 Object Diagrams (if any); 4.7 System Implementation: requirements (hardware, software), program development, system testing (test plan, test data, actual versus expected results, performance evaluation, limitations), system security (password protection, authentication, digital signature, cryptography — if any), training, documentation, system conversion (changeover and recommended procedure).
source: Computer Science MSc/PhD Documentation Format, Chapter Four

text: Chapter Five: Summary, Conclusion and Recommendation — 5.1 Summary; 5.2 Conclusion; 5.3 Recommendation (5.3.1 Application Areas; 5.3.2 Suggestion for Further Research); 5.4 Contribution to Knowledge (MSc and PhD only). Followed by REFERENCES and Appendices: A Program Listings; B Sample Outputs; C Questionnaire (where applicable).
source: Computer Science MSc/PhD Documentation Format, Chapter Five and back matter

section: Precedence — Manual of Style and Computer Science format
text: The UNIZIK Manual of Style 2019 governs everything in a Computer Science thesis (preliminary pages, Chapter One and Chapter Two structure, formatting including double line spacing and margins, citation, referencing, headings, tables and figures) EXCEPT the section structure of Chapters Three, Four and Five, which follows the Computer Science department's documentation format.
source: Project rule: precedence confirmed by the project owner
